issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25858 - Fixed reply form showing parent comment author's details
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR fixes a real bug: the reply form header showed the parent comment author's name and expertise whenever the logged-in member had no name or expertise set. It does this by removing the `comment?.member` fallbacks in `FormWrapper` and `Form`, and it drops the now-unused `comment` prop from `FormWrapper`. The header fix itself is correct and the two new e2e tests reproduce the reported scenario.

The PR also goes beyond that fix in three ways that matter. First, `FormWrapper` now dereferences `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but `MainForm` renders `FormWrapper` without an `openForm`. Focusing the top-level comment box will throw. Second, the editor's editable gate changes from "has a name" to "has expertise", which locks out members who have a name but no expertise, even though the details popup allows that. Third, the reply submit now sends `in_reply_to_id: parent.id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`, which re-targets reply-to-reply submissions to the top-level comment.

I would not merge this as-is. The crash and the two behavioral regressions need fixing, and the tests should cover the main form and reply-to-reply paths.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The header fix is correct, but the PR introduces a crash on the main comment form (any focus or typing in the top-level box throws during render). It also silently changes editing permissions for name-only members and changes the persisted in-reply-to target for reply-to-reply submissions. None of these are covered by the new tests. The crash and both regressions should be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Comment threads are rendered by comment.tsx. A reply button on a comment opens a ReplyForm (reply-form.tsx) that wraps the shared Form and FormWrapper from forms/form.tsx. The same FormWrapper is also used by MainForm (main-form.tsx) for the top-level comment box. FormWrapper draws the member avatar, name and expertise header and the padding for the open state. Form owns the TipTap editor's editable state, which is currently tied to the member's name and expertise. On submit, ReplyForm dispatches addReply in actions.ts, which posts the comment through GhostApi and merges the result back into the comment tree.

This PR changes three pieces of that flow. It removes the fallback to the parent comment's name and expertise from the header, which fixes the reported bug. It makes the editor editable only when the member has expertise, which is a new gate. And it changes the in_reply_to_id value sent on submit from the openForm state to the top-level parent's id. The third change is not described in the PR and alters what gets persisted.
steps: Start at the entry point: comment.tsx PublishedComment computes openForm and renders ReplyFormBox, which renders ReplyForm with parent set to the top-level comment. The reply-to-reply target lives in openForm.in_reply_to_id, set at comment.tsx line 110.
ReplyForm (reply-form.tsx) builds the submit handler. This PR changes in_reply_to_id from openForm.in_reply_to_id to parent.id, and it removes the comment prop from FormWrapper.

FormWrapper (form.tsx ~line 299) renders the header from member.name and member.expertise only. This removes the parent-comment fallback that caused the bug. It is also reached from MainForm (main-form.tsx line 98), which passes no openForm, and this PR makes that path throw when open.

Form (form.tsx ~line 244-265) toggles the editor through editor.setEditable. The gate is now member.expertise rather than member.name, which affects every entry point that uses Form, including the top-level box.

findings.title: Focusing the top-level comment box throws during render
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx`, inside `FormWrapper` around line 313, `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` dereferences a prop that is optional and is not passed by `MainForm` (`main-form.tsx` line 98). Focusing or typing in the top-level comment box then throws during render. Change it back to optional chaining (`openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`), matching the original code. Then run the comments-ui typecheck to confirm strict mode passes, and add an e2e check that focusing the main comment box doesn't throw.

findings.title: Editor is now locked for members who have a name but no expertise
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx` around lines 261-265, the `useEffect` that calls `editor.setEditable` was changed from gating on `memberName` to `member?.expertise`. The add-details popup only requires a name (`add-details-popup.tsx` submit checks `name.trim()`), so name-only members are now locked out of editing and get re-locked after saving their name. Restore the name-based gate (`!!member?.name`) and make the dependency array match. Keep the header change, which correctly removes the `comment?.member` fallbacks. Update the stale comment on line 263 to match.

findings.title: Reply-to-reply submissions now point at the top-level comment
findings.body:
The submit payload changed from `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`:

::diff{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx" lines="24-40"}

The two values differ when someone replies to a reply. `openReplyForm` in `comment.tsx` (lines 107-111) sets `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to the specific reply being answered, and `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` shows its text in the "Reply to" header. But `ReplyForm` receives `parent` as the top-level comment (`comment.tsx` lines 248-251). So after this change, a reply-to-reply gets saved as a reply to the top-level comment while the UI still says it is replying to the other reply. The stored thread structure no longer matches what the user chose.

This also changes direct replies to top-level comments. `openForm.in_reply_to_id` is undefined there, so the old payload had no `in_reply_to_id`. The new payload sets it to the parent's id.

The PR description doesn't mention this change, and the tests don't exercise it. Restore the original value and keep `openForm` in the dependency array.

::suggestion{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx" lines="30-30"}
                in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id,
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx`, the `submit` callback (around lines 24-35) was changed to send `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`. `parent` is the top-level comment, but `openForm.in_reply_to_id` is the reply the user is answering (set in `comment.tsx` lines 107-111). Revert to `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` and restore `openForm` in the `useCallback` dependency array. This change is not part of the header fix, so keep it out of this PR.

findings.title: New e2e tests don't cover the paths that regressed
findings.body:
Both new tests exercise only the reply-form header with the parent-fallback bug. Neither covers what this PR actually changed in behavior:

- **Main form focus**: nothing focuses the top-level `main-form` box, so the `openForm` crash (finding 1) never runs.
- **Name without expertise**: nothing checks whether a name-only member can type, so the editable-gate regression (finding 2) goes unnoticed.
- **Reply-to-reply submit**: nothing asserts the `in_reply_to_id` sent to `addReply`, so finding 3 goes unnoticed.

The second test is also weak. `not.toHaveText('Named Author')` passes on any empty or "Anonymous" header. Asserting the exact expected text (`'Anonymous'`, since `name` is null) would catch regressions better.

::code{file="apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts" lines="651-680"}

Add a focused test for the main box, a name-only test that types into the editor, and a reply-to-reply submit assertion on the `in_reply_to_id` payload.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` (new tests around lines 614-680), add coverage for the paths this PR changes. (1) Focus the top-level main-form editor and assert no error occurs. (2) Set a member with a name but null expertise, then assert the reply editor accepts typing. (3) Reply to a reply and assert the submitted `in_reply_to_id` equals the reply's id, not the top-level comment's. Also make the "does not inherit name" test assert the exact expected header text ('Anonymous') instead of `not.toHaveText`. Follow the existing helpers in the file (`initializeTest`, `waitEditorFocused`, `buildMember`).

findings.title: Comment above the editable gate contradicts the code
findings.body:
The comment says "Disable editing if the member doesn't have a name", but the code now checks `member?.expertise`. Whoever reads this next will be misled about which rule is intended. Update it along with whatever gate is finally chosen (see finding 2).

::code{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx" lines="262-265"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx` around line 263, the comment above `editor.setEditable(...)` says editing is disabled when the member has no name, but the code (line 264) checks `member?.expertise`. Once the gate is decided (see the editability finding), make the comment and the condition agree.

findings.title: Unrelated class-name reorder in reply form
findings.body:
The PR changes `className='mt-[-16px] pr-2'` to `className='pr-2 mt-[-16px]'`. This is a pure reordering with no effect on rendering, and it is outside the bug being fixed. It adds noise to the diff. Revert it so the review stays focused on the actual change.

::diff{file="apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx" lines="47-47"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx` line 47, the wrapper `className` was reordered from `'mt-[-16px] pr-2'` to `'pr-2 mt-[-16px]'`. This has no effect and is unrelated to the fix. Restore the original order.
